relevance_reason: Case report of bilateral pheochromocytoma with a germline TMEM127 variant; adds a further patient to PPGL8.

findings.statement: Delgado et al. (2022) reported a 65-year-old woman with hypertension, bilateral adrenal nodules on CT scan, and elevated urinary metanephrines, consistent with bilateral pheochromocytoma. She underwent laparoscopic bilateral adrenalectomy, and no recurrence was recorded after 5 years of follow-up.
quotes: We report a 65 year old woman with hypertension, bilateral adrenal nodules found in the CT scan and elevated urinary metanephrines.
She was subjected to a laparoscopic bilateral adrenal excision. After five years of follow up, no recurrence of the disease has been recorded.

findings.statement: In a 65-year-old woman with bilateral pheochromocytoma, Delgado et al. (2022) identified a mutation in the TMEM127 gene, c.117_120delGTCT, by genetic testing.
quotes: Her genetic testing showed a c.117_120delGTCT TMEM127 gene mutation.

relevance_reason: This is a case report of a TMEM127 intronic variant of uncertain significance in a patient with a neck paraganglioma and acromegaly. It adds possible but unconfirmed evidence for PPGL8.

findings.statement: Stütz et al. (2020) reported a 61-year-old woman with a 4 x 4 x 6 cm paraganglioma in the left supraclavicular fossa. It showed MIBG uptake, plasma free metanephrines were normal, and histology was positive for synaptophysin and chromogranin. She also had acromegaly from a 13-mm GH-secreting pituitary macroadenoma. She had paroxysmal hypertensive crises, which the authors attributed to the acromegaly, and multinodular goiter; her family history was unremarkable. Both tumors were cured by surgery, and she remained well after 10 years of follow-up.
quotes: A 61-year-old female patient presented with pressure in the left neck, deepening of the voice and exertional dyspnoea existing for about half a year.
Plasma free metanephrines were in the normal range on two occasions. 123I-MIBG-scintigraphy and SPECT/CT demonstrated enhancement of the tumour and possibility of PGL was confirmed
MRI scan showed a 13 mm pituitary macroadenoma on the left side

findings.statement: In this patient, next-generation sequencing of PPGL susceptibility genes found a heterozygous intronic TMEM127 variant, c.245-10C>G in intron 2. It is absent from gnomAD and was classified as a variant of uncertain significance under ACMG criteria. Segregation could not be studied: her parents were deceased and her children declined testing. Because the variant lies between other known variants at c.245-7 and c.245-12, the authors suggested that it might disrupt the consensus splice site, but they noted that experimental confirmation was needed.
quotes: This resulted in the detection of a heterozygous mutation in the TMEM127 gene on intron 2 (c.245-10C>G), which was a novel variant at that time

The identified TMEM127 variant (c.245-10C>G) is a variant of uncertain significance according to ACMG criteria (; PM2, as variant is not found in gnomAD database, and BP4, based on in silicio prediction tools).
Its location between the other known variants c.245-7 (splice region) and c.245-12 (intron) suggests the possibility of a relevant variant with disruption of the consensus splice site.

relevance_reason: A large genotype-phenotype review of germline TMEM127 variants in people with pheochromocytoma, paraganglioma and renal cell carcinoma. Only the abstract was available.

findings.statement: Armaiz-Pena et al. (2021) studied 110 index patients carrying germline TMEM127 variants. The data came from a registry, published reports and public databases. Mean age was 45 years (range, 21-84 years), and females outnumbered males (76 vs 34, P < .001). Most patients had pheochromocytoma (94; 85.5%). Paraganglioma (10; 9%) and renal cell carcinoma (6; 5.4%) also occurred, either alone or together with pheochromocytoma. One-third of patients had multiple tumors, 15.4% had a known family history, and metastatic disease was rare (2.8%).
quotes: The cohort comprised 110 index patients (111 variants) with a mean age of 45 years (range, 21-84 years). Females were predominant (76 vs 34, P < .001).
Most patients had PHEO (n = 94; 85.5%), although PGL (n = 10; 9%) and renal cell carcinoma (RCC, n = 6; 5.4%) were also detected, either alone or in combination with PHEO.
One-third of the cases had multiple tumors, and known family history was reported in 15.4%. Metastatic PHEO/PGL was rare (2.8%).

findings.statement: Armaiz-Pena et al. (2021) reported that 82% of the catecholamine profiles of pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas in TMEM127 variant carriers involved epinephrine, either alone or combined with norepinephrine.
quotes: Epinephrine alone, or combined with norepinephrine, accounted for 82% of the catecholamine profiles of PHEO/PGLs.

findings.statement: Armaiz-Pena et al. (2021) found that most TMEM127 variants (n = 63) occurred only once and 13 were recurrent (2-12 times). Truncating variants were more common overall. Nontruncating variants, however, predominated in presentations other than pheochromocytoma alone (36% in pheochromocytoma-only vs 69% in other presentations, P < .001). They also clustered disproportionately within the transmembrane regions (P < .01). Combining clinical and earlier experimental data, the authors proposed sorting variants into 4 groups by mutation type, location and predicted disruption.
quotes: Most variants (n = 63) occurred only once and 13 were recurrent (2-12 times).

Although nontruncating variants were less frequent than truncating changes overall, they were predominant in non-PHEO clinical presentations (36% PHEO-only vs 69% other, P < .001) and clustered disproportionately within transmembrane regions (P < .01)
Integration of clinical and previous experimental data supported classification of variants into 4 groups based on mutation type, localization, and predicted disruption.

findings.statement: Armaiz-Pena et al. (2021) concluded that patients with TMEM127 variants often resemble those with sporadic nonmetastatic pheochromocytoma. Paraganglioma and renal cell carcinoma may also occur, although the authors stated that the causal link requires further evaluation.
quotes: Patients with TMEM127 variants often resemble sporadic nonmetastatic PHEOs. PGL and RCC may also co-occur, although their causal link requires further evaluation.

relevance_reason: The abstract covers registry patients with germline mutations in SDHA, TMEM127, MAX and SDHAF2. It does not name or address the gene behind PPGL8, so it only gives context on hereditary pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma susceptibility genes.

findings.statement: Bausch et al. (2017) studied 972 unrelated registrants of the European-American-Asian Pheochromocytoma-Paraganglioma Registry who had no mutations in the classic pheochromocytoma- and paraganglioma-associated genes. Of these, 58 (6.0%) carried germline mutations in newer susceptibility genes: 29 in SDHA, 20 in TMEM127, 8 in MAX, and 1 in SDHAF2. Fifty-three of the 58 patients (91%) had familial, multiple, extra-adrenal, and/or malignant tumors and/or were younger than 40 years.
quotes: Of 972 unrelated registrants without mutations in the classic pheochromocytoma- and paraganglioma-associated genes
58 (6.0%) carried germline mutations of interest, including 29 SDHA, 20 TMEM127, 8 MAX, and 1 SDHAF2
Fifty-three of 58 patients (91%) had familial, multiple, extra-adrenal, and/or malignant tumors and/or were younger than 40 years.

findings.statement: Bausch et al. (2017) found 7 malignant pheochromocytomas/paragangliomas among 63 tumors (11%) in patients with SDHA or TMEM127 mutations. Extra-adrenal tumors occurred in 28 mutation carriers (48%), including 23 of 29 SDHA carriers (79%), particularly as head and neck paragangliomas. SDHA-related disease began as early as 8 years of age. MAX-related tumors occurred almost exclusively in the adrenal glands and were frequently bilateral.
quotes: Newly uncovered are 7 of 63 (11%) malignant pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas in SDHA and TMEM127 disease. SDHA disease occurred as early as 8 years of age.
Extra-adrenal tumors occurred in 28 mutation carriers (48%) and in 23 of 29 SDHA mutation carriers (79%), particularly with head and neck paraganglioma.
MAX disease occurred almost exclusively in the adrenal glands with frequently bilateral tumors.

findings.statement: Bausch et al. (2017) estimated the penetrance of SDHA mutations at 39% by age 40 years. Penetrance differed significantly between index patients (45%) and mutation-carrying relatives (13%; P less than 0.001).
quotes: Penetrance in the largest subset, SDHA carriers, was 39% at 40 years of age and is statistically different in index patients (45%) vs mutation-carrying relatives (13%; P < .001).

findings.statement: Bausch et al. (2017) recommended genetic testing for SDHA, TMEM127, MAX, and SDHAF2 in patients at high clinical risk whose classic susceptibility genes are mutation negative. They also recommended regular, systematic whole-body investigation for gene-specific prevention and early detection.
quotes: Genetic testing is recommended in patients at clinically high risk if the classic genes are mutation negative.
Gene-specific prevention and/or early detection requires regular, systematic whole-body investigation.

relevance_reason: Reports a large six-generation family with a germline TMEM127 mutation and defines the penetrance and clinical features of TMEM127-related pheochromocytoma (PPGL8).

findings.statement: Toledo et al. (2015) offered clinical and genetic screening to 151 individuals from a six-generation family that carried a germline TMEM127 mutation. Of 34 mutation carriers with clinical data, followed for 8.7 +/- 8.1 years, 11 (32%) were diagnosed with pheochromocytoma at a median age of 43 years. In 9 patients symptoms began at 29 years (range, 10-55 years), and 2 patients were asymptomatic. Tumors were multicentric in 5 patients (45%) and bilateral in 5 (45%). Six patients (54%) had at least one adrenomedullary nodule smaller than 10 mm. No paragangliomas, distant metastases, or other manifestations were found.
quotes: Clinical data were obtained from 34 TMEM127-mutation carriers followed up for 8.7 ± 8.1 years (range, 1-20 y). Pheochromocytoma was diagnosed in 11 carriers (32%) at a median age of 43 years.
Tumors were multicentric in five (45%) and bilateral in five (45%) patients. Six patients (54%) had at least one adrenomedullary nodule less than 10 mm.
No paragangliomas, distant metastases, or other manifestations were detected.

findings.statement: Toledo et al. (2015) found that 47 members of a six-generation family with pheochromocytoma carried the germline TMEM127 c.410-2A>C mutation, which affects a splice site.
quotes: Forty seven individuals carried the c.410-2A>C TMEM127 mutation.

findings.statement: In this family, Toledo et al. (2015) estimated that the cumulative penetrance of pheochromocytoma in TMEM127 mutation carriers was 0% at ages 0-20 years, 3% at 21-30 years, 15% at 31-40 years, 24% at 41-50 years, and 32% at 51-65 years. The youngest patient was diagnosed at age 22 years, and the earliest symptoms were reported at age 10.
quotes: Cumulative penetrance of pheochromocytoma was 0% at 0-20 years, 3% at 21-30 years, 15% at 31-40 years, 24% at 41-50 years, and 32% at 51-65 years.
The youngest case was diagnosed at 22 years and the earliest symptoms were reported at age 10.

findings.statement: Toledo et al. (2015) described tumor multicentricity, nodular adrenomedullary hyperplasia, and symptom onset more than a decade before diagnosis as novel findings in TMEM127-related pheochromocytoma. They recommended offering TMEM127 genetic testing to at-risk individuals at age 22 years and annual clinical surveillance for mutation carriers.
quotes: Tumor multicentricity, nodular adrenomedullary hyperplasia, and the occurrence of symptoms more than a decade earlier than the age at diagnosis are novel findings in TMEM127-related PHEO.
We thus recommend that TMEM127 genetic testing should be offered to at-risk individuals at age 22 years and mutation carriers should undergo clinical surveillance annually.

relevance_reason: Reports germline TMEM127 mutations in patients with bilateral pheochromocytoma, the gene underlying PPGL8.

findings.statement: Takeichi et al. (2012) sequenced TMEM127 in germline DNA from 74 unrelated Japanese patients with pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma who were negative for mutations and deletions in RET, VHL, SDHB and SDHD. They found the same heterozygous germline 4-bp deletion (c.116_119delTGTC; p.Ile41ArgfsX39) in 2 unrelated patients (2.7%) with bilateral adrenal pheochromocytoma. Tumor DNA showed loss of heterozygosity from a 2q deletion. The deletion had been reported before in a Brazilian patient and was not found in 114 healthy ethnically matched controls.
quotes: Among the 74 eligible patients, two unrelated patients (2·7%) with bilateral adrenal pheochromocytoma were found to have an identical germline TMEM127 mutation (c.116_119delTGTC, p.Ile41ArgfsX39) associated with 2q deletion loss of heterozygosity
We also determined that none of the 114 normal healthy controls had this deletion mutation.

74 unrelated patients with pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma who tested negative for mutations and deletions in RET, VHL, SDHB and SDHD were recruited through a multi-institutional collaborative effort in Japan

findings.statement: Takeichi et al. (2012) found that the germline TMEM127 deletion occurred together with loss of heterozygosity from a 2q deletion in tumor DNA. They noted that this fits TMEM127 acting as a tumor suppressor gene.
quotes: tumour DNA was analysed for the loss of heterozygosity
this is consistent with its function as a tumour suppressor gene

findings.statement: Takeichi et al. (2012) presented their study as the first report of a pathologic role for TMEM127 mutation in pheochromocytoma in an Asian population. They found TMEM127 mutations in 2.7% of Japanese patients who were negative for RET, VHL, SDHB and SDHD mutations. They concluded that the prevalence and phenotype appeared similar to those in earlier studies.
quotes: This is the first report showing that TMEM127 mutation plays a pathological role in pheochromocytoma in an Asian population.
Although our surveillance is limited, the prevalence and the phenotype of this gene mutation appear to be similar to those reported in previous studies.

relevance_reason: Large multicenter screen of TMEM127 in pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma that reports germline mutation prevalence, clinical correlations and functional localization studies. It directly characterizes PPGL caused by TMEM127.

findings.statement: Yao et al. (2010) sequenced the TMEM127 gene in 990 individuals with pheochromocytoma and/or paraganglioma from 8 worldwide referral centers. The cohort included 898 previously unreported cases without mutations in other susceptibility genes. They identified 19 potentially pathogenic germline TMEM127 mutations in 20 independent families. A multiplex PCR-based method was used to screen 545 samples for large gene deletions, and none were found.
quotes: We sequenced the FP/TMEM127 gene in 990 individuals with pheochromocytomas and/or paragangliomas, including 898 previously unreported cases without mutations in other susceptibility genes from 8 independent worldwide referral centers
We identified 19 potentially pathogenic FP/TMEM127 germline mutations in 20 independent families, but no large deletions were detected.

findings.statement: Yao et al. (2010) found that all TMEM127 mutation carriers had adrenal tumors. Seven had bilateral tumors (P = 2.7 x 10(-4)), and 5 of 20 had familial disease (P = .005). Median age at onset was 41.5 years in carriers and 45 years in patients without a mutation, which was not significantly different (P = .54). The most common presentation was a single benign adrenal tumor in a patient older than 40 years, and malignancy occurred in 1 carrier (5%). The authors concluded that germline TMEM127 mutations were associated with pheochromocytoma but not paraganglioma, and that they occurred in an age group often excluded from genetic screening algorithms.
quotes: All mutation carriers had adrenal tumors, including 7 bilateral (P = 2.7 × 10(-4)) and/or with familial disease (5 of 20 samples; P = .005).
The most common presentation was that of a single benign adrenal tumor in patients older than 40 years. Malignancy was seen in 1 mutation carrier (5%).
Germline mutations of FP/TMEM127 were associated with pheochromocytoma but not paraganglioma and occurred in an age group frequently excluded from genetic screening algorithms.

findings.statement: Yao et al. (2010) expressed 5 novel TMEM127 mutants in cell lines and used confocal microscopy to compare them with wild type. The mutant proteins were diffusely localized, whereas wild-type TMEM127 showed a discrete multiorganelle distribution. The authors concluded that disease-associated mutations disrupt the intracellular distribution of the protein.
quotes: Expression of 5 novel FP/TMEM127 mutations in cell lines revealed diffuse localization of the mutant proteins in contrast with the discrete multiorganelle distribution of wild-type TMEM127.
Disease-associated mutations disrupt intracellular distribution of the FP/TMEM127 protein.

relevance_reason: This paper first identifies germline TMEM127 mutations as the cause of familial and sporadic-appearing pheochromocytoma. It describes the patients, the variants and functional evidence of a tumor suppressor mechanism that acts through mTOR.

findings.statement: Qin et al. (2010) had previously mapped a familial pheochromocytoma susceptibility locus (FP) to chromosome 2q11. Further affected relatives and additional linked families narrowed the locus to a 19.62-Mb region containing 205 genes.
quotes: we previously defined a novel pheochromocytoma susceptibility locus to chromosome 2q11, which we named FP (Familial Pheochromocytoma)
additional linked families redefined the limits of the FP locus to a region containing 205 genes (NCBI Build 35.1, Suppl. Table 1) spanning 19.62Mb between 94,81Mbp and 114,43Mbp

findings.statement: Qin et al. (2010) found that the affected individuals in the original FP kindred showed a dominant pattern of transmission. Four mutation carriers in Family 1 had no clinical disease at ages 43 to 58 years, which suggests incomplete penetrance.
quotes: Identification of other affected individuals in the original kindred established a dominant model of transmission
Four mutation carriers from Family 1 (Table 1) remain without clinical disease at 43 to 58 years of age

findings.statement: Qin et al. (2010) sequenced exons of genes in the FP locus using tumor DNA from the index case of Family 1. They identified a splice-site mutation in TMEM127, IVS3-2A>C (p.Leu138fs), predicted to produce a truncated 148-amino acid protein. The mutation was present in the germline and in all 6 other affected sibs, and absent from 2 unaffected sibs. The same mutation was found in a second, unrelated family (Family 5), and haplotype analysis excluded a common ancestor.
quotes: we identified a splice-site variant (IVS3-2A>C) in the provisional transmembrane-encoding gene, TMEM127, also known as FLJ20507
This mutation was also present in this patient’s germline DNA as well as in each of six other affected siblings, but not in samples from two unaffected sibs.
One of the identified mutations, IVS3-2A>C, was detected in two separate families (Table 1, families 1 and 5). Haplotype analysis of tumor DNA excluded a common ancestor

findings.statement: Qin et al. (2010) sequenced TMEM127 in 102 additional index pheochromocytoma cases (19 familial, 83 apparently sporadic) and found 6 additional mutations. Overall, 4 TMEM127 variants were found among 12 families without mutations in other susceptibility genes (about 30% of familial cases), and 3 were found among sporadic-appearing cases (about 3%). All mutations were germline, and none were present in 1,064 ethnically matched control alleles. Six of the 7 variants were splice-site or nonsense (truncating) mutations.
quotes: We next sequenced germline and/or tumor DNA from an additional 102 index pheochromocytomas, 19 of which had a clear familial history, and 83 were apparently sporadic cases.
we detected truncating germline TMEM127 mutations in approximately 30% of familial tumors and about 3% of sporadic-appearing pheochromocytomas without a known genetic cause
None of the sequence changes found in the pheochromocytoma samples were identified in a control group of 1064 ethnically-matched alleles

findings.statement: Qin et al. (2010) identified a heterozygous germline 1-bp insertion in TMEM127, c.150insA (p.Pro51fs), predicted to produce a 106-amino acid protein. The patient was adopted, so family history was unknown, and had a unilateral adrenal pheochromocytoma at age 25.
quotes: 2 | U | A | 25 | 1(1) | 0 (0/1) | c.150insA (p.Pro51fs) | insertion | 106aa
One of the patients was adopted and thus heredity status was unknown (patient 2, Table1)

findings.statement: Qin et al. (2010) identified a heterozygous nonsense mutation in TMEM127, c.475C>T (p.Gln159X), in a family with 2 affected members (Family 3). Both had bilateral adrenal pheochromocytomas (4 tumors in total), with onset between ages 48 and 72.

Qin et al. (2010) identified a heterozygous 4-bp deletion in TMEM127, c.264-267delCAGA (p.Thr89fs), predicted to produce a 121-amino acid protein. The patient had no family history of pheochromocytoma and developed bilateral adrenal tumors at age 46.
quotes: 4 | N | A | 46 | 1(2) | 100 (1/1) | c.264- 267delCAGA (p.Thr89fs) | deletion | 121aa

findings.statement: Qin et al. (2010) identified a heterozygous splice-site mutation in TMEM127, IVS2-1G>T (p.Phe83fs), predicted to produce a 99-amino acid protein. The family (Family 6) had 2 affected members, both with bilateral adrenal pheochromocytoma and onset between ages 54 and 66.
quotes: 6 | Y | A | 54-66 | 2(2) | 100 (2/2) | IVS2-1G>T (p.Phe83fs) | splice site | 99aa

findings.statement: Qin et al. (2010) identified a heterozygous missense mutation in TMEM127, c.268G>A (p.Val90Met), in a patient with no family history who had a unilateral adrenal pheochromocytoma at age 32. The affected residue is conserved among putative mammalian orthologs. Only germline DNA was available, so LOH could not be assessed.
quotes: The only missense mutation (V90M) in this series targeted an amino acid conserved amongst putative mammalian TMEM127 orthologs. As only germline DNA was available from this sample, LOH status could not be determined.

findings.statement: Qin et al. (2010) reported a mean age at diagnosis of 45.3 years for pheochromocytoma in patients with TMEM127 mutations. This is similar to sporadic cases and older than syndromic cases. All tumors arose from the adrenal medulla, about half of patients had bilateral tumors, and no malignancy or recurrence was seen during 4 to 16 years of follow-up.
quotes: Clinically, patients with TMEM127 mutations developed pheochromocytomas on average at 45.3 years of age, similar to the mean age at diagnosis of sporadic pheochromocytomas (43.6-43.9y,) but notably older than syndromic cases (24.9-30.2y,).
All tumors arose from the adrenal medulla and were bilateral in approximately half of the patients (Table 1).
No malignancies, defined by the presence of metastasis in nonchromaffin-derived tissues, or recurrences, were detected during follow-up of the affected cases (4 to 16 years).

findings.statement: Qin et al. (2010) examined loss of heterozygosity (LOH) at the TMEM127 locus in 35 pheochromocytomas. All 19 TMEM127-mutant tumors tested showed LOH with loss of the wild-type allele, compared with 2 of 16 wild-type tumors, consistent with a 2-hit tumor suppressor mechanism. TMEM127 expression was 4-fold lower in mutant tumors, which the authors suggested reflected instability of the mutant transcript.
quotes: all TMEM127-mutant tumors tested (n=19, including multiple affected individuals from the same family or bilateral tumors) had LOH, in contrast with only 2 of 16 wild-type TMEM127 samples (P=5.17e-8, Suppl. Table 5)
In each mutant TMEM127 pheochromocytoma, the wild-type allele was lost (Suppl.Fig.2A), in agreement with a two-hit model of tumor suppressor inactivation.
This degree of downregulation suggests instability of the mutant transcript, rather than low expression simply due to loss of one allele.

findings.statement: Qin et al. (2010) found that no protein product was detectable in HEK293 cells transfected with mutant TMEM127 constructs (M158 and M99), despite equivalent transfection efficiency. This supports a loss-of-function effect.
quotes: However, we were unable to detect a translation product from the mutant constructs in these cell lines (Fig.1A), despite equivalent transfection efficiencies (Suppl. Fig.4A). These data suggest that TMEM127-mutant proteins are not expressed, in support of a loss-of-function effect of these variants.

findings.statement: Qin et al. (2010) found by expression profiling that TMEM127-mutant pheochromocytomas clustered with NF1- and RET-mutant tumors and were enriched for kinase receptor signaling transcripts, not hypoxia transcripts. TMEM127-mutant tumors showed increased S6K phosphorylation compared with normal adrenal medulla and TMEM127 wild-type tumors.
quotes: we confirmed the cluster association between the TMEM127-mutant tumors and pheochromocytomas with NF1 and RET mutations
we examined lysates from TMEM127-mutant pheochromocytomas and found increased phosphorylation of S6K compared to normal adrenal medulla or tumors without a TMEM127 mutation

findings.statement: Qin et al. (2010) found that TMEM127 knockdown increased phosphorylation of the mTORC1 targets 4EBP1 and S6K, increased cell size and increased proliferation. Overexpression of TMEM127 reduced mTORC1 signaling and proliferation, without affecting RAS activity or AKT phosphorylation. TMEM127 localized to the plasma membrane, early endosomes, Golgi and lysosomes, and colocalized with amino acid-activated perinuclear mTOR, suggesting that it is a compartment-specific negative regulator of mTORC1.
quotes: In contrast, TMEM127 knockdown led to increased phosphorylation of 4EBP1 in various cell lines (Fig.3D).
we found that TMEM127 knockdown cells were larger (Fig. 3H, Suppl. Fig.7D) and proliferated at increased rates compared to control cell lines
We found that TMEM127 localized to the same cellular compartment as that of amino acid-activated mTOR (Fig 4C).

relevance_reason: The abstract describes a familial pheochromocytoma syndrome with no known genetic defect. The authors used linkage and LOH analysis to map it to two susceptibility loci (2cen and 16p13) and proposed digenic recessive inheritance. This is background mapping and heterogeneity evidence for familial pheochromocytoma, but the abstract does not name a gene.

findings.statement: Dahia et al. (2005) studied a family with pheochromocytoma that had no known genetic defect. Multipoint parametric linkage analysis gave identical LOD scores of 2.97 for loci at chromosome 2cen and 16p13. A two-locus parametric linkage analysis gave a maximum LOD score of 5.16 under a double recessive multiplicative model, which the authors suggested meant both loci were required for the disease to develop.
quotes: Multipoint parametric linkage analysis revealed identical LOD scores of 2.97 for chromosome 2cen and 16p13 loci.
A two-locus parametric linkage analysis produced maximum LOD score of 5.16 under a double recessive multiplicative model, suggesting that both loci are required to develop the disease.

findings.statement: Dahia et al. (2005) described a familial pheochromocytoma syndrome that they considered consistent with digenic inheritance. They concluded that it added a recessive digenic trait to the genetic heterogeneity of these tumors.
quotes: We describe here a familial pheochromocytoma syndrome consistent with digenic inheritance identified through a combination of global genomics strategies.
adds a recessive digenic trait to the increasingly broad genetic heterogeneity of these tumors

findings.statement: Dahia et al. (2005) detected allele-specific loss of heterozygosity (LOH) only at the chromosome 2 locus in all tumors from the family, which they considered consistent with a tumor suppressor gene. Transcription profiling identified 4 additional pheochromocytomas with a similar genetic pattern, which helped refine the chromosome 2 locus. High-density SNP-array LOH mapping found LOH within the chromosome 2 region in 18 of 62 pheochromocytomas, narrowing the locus to less than 2 cM.
quotes: Allele-specific loss of heterozygosity (LOH) was detected only at the chromosome 2 locus in all tumors from this family, consistent with a tumor suppressor gene.
Four additional pheochromocytomas with a similar genetic pattern were identified through transcription profiling and helped refine the chromosome 2 locus.

High-density LOH mapping with single nucleotide polymorphism-based array identified a total of 18 of 62 pheochromocytomas with LOH within the chromosome 2 region, which further narrowed down the locus to <2 cM.

findings.statement: Dahia et al. (2005) noted that pheochromocytomas result from mutations in at least 6 different genes, each part of a distinct autosomal dominant disorder, but that some families with pheochromocytoma have no known genetic defect. They concluded that their study provided evidence for 2 novel pheochromocytoma susceptibility loci.
quotes: However, there remain familial occurrences of pheochromocytoma without a known genetic defect.
This finding provides evidence for two novel susceptibility loci for pheochromocytoma
